key_insight: Domain-specific biomedical embeddings, especially BioBERT, helped identify clinical trial protocols at elevated dosing-error risk better than a ClinicalBERT baseline.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier safety screening of trial protocols and help teams prioritize review of dosing plans before patient exposure.
method: Encoded clinical trial text with transformer models such as ClinicalBERT, PubMedBERT, BioBERT, and MedCPT.
Combined text embeddings with categorical metadata features.
Compared classical machine learning and neural network classifiers for dosage-error prediction.
evidence_signal: Using ROC-AUC, BioBERT reached 0.794 with logistic regression, and the strongest models achieved 0.821 to 0.853 for dosing-error prediction.
watch_item: The findings come from model benchmarking on protocol data, so real-world deployment still needs external validation and careful review for dataset shift.
paper_title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models
